title: Week 7 Analysis
subtitle: Hume takes the lead. Cadegn's perfect NFC East is gone.
intro_paragraphs: The Eagles slipped from second to third in the NFC East, and that one move ended Cadegn's three-week run in first. Cadegn lost 19 points in that division alone, and Hume moved to the top with 49. Five divisions changed order: all four in the NFC, plus the AFC North again. Only 14 points now separate first from last, the closest the pool has been all season.

Washington, Buffalo, the Chargers, and Jacksonville had their byes this week. They've played six games, and so have Carolina, Minnesota, Detroit, Miami, Cincinnati, and Kansas City after earlier byes.

fun_facts.heading: Hume Takes the Lead
fun_facts.body: Hume gained 6 to reach 49: 3 when the Cowboys moved into second in the NFC East, and 3 when the Cardinals fell back into last in the NFC West. It's the first time Hume has led this season. Hume is the fifth different leader in seven weeks, after Dustin, Dilger, Tom, and Cadegn. Mike T and Farmer haven't led yet.

fun_facts.heading: Cadegn's Perfect NFC East Breaks
fun_facts.body: Cadegn had the NFC East exactly right through Week 6: Giants, Eagles, Cowboys, Commanders. It was the only perfect division anyone had outside the AFC East. The Eagles fell to 2-5, the Cowboys moved into second at 3-4, and the division went from 25 points to 6. Cadegn got 9 back from the Bears moving into second and the Saints and Cardinals both falling back into last, so the net was -10, to 46. Cadegn is 3 behind Hume and still has 3 of 8 division-winner picks currently correct, the most in the pool.

fun_facts.heading: Mike T and Cadegn Tied at 46
fun_facts.body: Mike T broke even. The Packers fell from second to last in the NFC North, which cost Mike T all 6 points there, and the Cowboys and Cardinals got 6 back. Mike T is ranked 2nd ahead of Cadegn on the second tiebreaker, with two top-2 bonuses (AFC East, and Chiefs-Broncos in the AFC West) to Cadegn's one. Tom gained 1 and is 4th at 43: the Bears and Cardinals were worth 3 each, but the Cowboys leaving third cost Tom 5, including the bottom-2 bonus.

fun_facts.heading: Farmer's Best Week
fun_facts.body: Farmer gained 14, the most in the pool this week and Farmer's best week of the season (the previous best was +13 in Week 2). The NFC East was worth 5: the Eagles in third and the Commanders in last, plus the bottom-2 bonus. The Saints dropping back into last gave Farmer back the 3 points they cost last week, and the Bears and Cardinals added 3 each. Last week Farmer was 35 out of first. Now it's 14. Farmer is still the only bettor without a perfect division, and everyone else has exactly one, the AFC East.

fun_facts.heading: Dilger and Dustin Can't Be Separated
fun_facts.body: Dilger gained 6 (Bears, Cardinals) and Dustin lost 6 (the Packers' fall cost 6, the Eagles leaving second cost 3, the Cardinals gave back 3). They meet at 37 and match on the first four tiebreakers: one perfect division, one top-2 bonus, one bottom-2 bonus, and 8 exact hits each. The fifth tiebreaker, the point-total guess, hasn't been set up yet, so they're officially tied for 5th.

fun_facts.heading: The AFC North Still Pays Nobody
fun_facts.body: The AFC North reshuffled for the second straight week, and nobody has an exact hit there again. The Browns and Steelers are 5-2, the Bengals moved up to third at 4-2, and the Ravens dropped to last at 4-3. Every bettor picked the Browns to finish last, and they're in first. The Ravens, the pick to win for Mike T, Dustin, and Tom, are now the team in last.

fun_facts.heading: The Locks: Back to Three
fun_facts.body:
With Arizona back in last, 3 of the 8 preseason unanimous picks are holding again: the Bills first, the Patriots second, and the Cardinals last. The Rams, the pool's unanimous pick to win the NFC West, climbed out of last to third at 3-4, 3 games behind the 6-1 49ers. The Lions, the unanimous pick in the NFC North, are third at 4-2 behind the 6-0 Vikings.

No division changed leaders this week, so the division-winner picks are where they were: Cadegn has 3 of 8, Mike T, Hume, and Farmer have 2, and Dilger, Dustin, and Tom have only the Bills.

closing_paragraph: One division turned over the top of the leaderboard. Hume leads by 3, the top four are within 6, and last place is 14 back. All four AFC North teams are within a game of each other, so it could shuffle again next week. Same time next Tuesday.
